Copilot CLI 1.0.106 changed the fences: "@-imports in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and copilot-instructions.md now follow Markdown code fence rules, so an import shown inside a nested code example is no longer pulled into the instructions and a real import after such an example is no longer dropped" (https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/blob/main/changelog.md). The changelog does not state the details, and the native resolver of 1.0.106 and of 1.0.107 (https://registry.npmjs.org/@github/copilot-linux-arm64/-/copilot-linux-arm64-1.0.107.tgz; repoDiscoverInstructionSources of prebuilds/linux-arm64/runtime.node in the asset copilot.tgz of the binary), run from Node on test workspaces without network on 2026-11-07, decides them, where 1.0.105 still read the earlier fences. A fence opens on a line that starts with at least three backticks or tildes after any whitespace (eight spaces open one), and not after > or a list marker. A line closes it only where it starts with at least as many of the same character after any whitespace and has only whitespace after them. Under ```` a line ``` closes nothing and under ``` a line ```` closes, ~~~ and ```js close nothing, and ``` with a space, a tab or U+00A0 after it closes. The end of the file closes it as well. A line with another backtick after a run of backticks opens no fence and reads as text with a code span, so ``` a`b opens none and ``` x`y ``` @a.md reads a.md, and a run of tildes can have either character after it. Only a line feed ends a line, and a carriage return is whitespace wherever it is. Whitespace is Unicode's White_Space: U+0085, U+00A0 and U+3000 indent a fence and end a path, and U+001C to U+001F and U+200B do neither, so @a.md<U+001C> looks up another file than a.md. An imported file's fences read the same.
